You are shown a snapshot of US macroeconomic and market data as it was known at the end of one month between 2007 and 2026.

Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
Industrial production is low versus its own 3-year history (-1.5) and the unemployment rate is low (-1.5), though it rose over the last 3 months. The national activity index is strongly positive (+2.0), which suggests a rebound after a weak patch. Headline CPI is low (-1.0) while core is modestly high.

The policy rate sits near its average and has fallen over 3 months. The 2-year yield rose over 3 months and the 10-year rose more, so the curve steepened. Long-end Treasuries are down over 3, 6 and 12 months. Gold is very weak, with a 3-month z of -2.0 and a 12-month z of -2.0.

One candidate is late 2016 to early 2017. Gold fell after the election, but the policy rate then was low and rising, so it doesn't fit a falling policy rate. A second candidate is late 2024. The Fed cut in Sept-Dec 2024, the 10-year rose sharply, and the curve steepened. But gold was strong then, so that doesn't fit.

A third candidate is mid-2013 (taper tantrum), when gold collapsed. Yet the policy rate was near zero, so a z-score of 0 with a 3-month fall doesn't fit well either.

A fourth candidate is the 2018-2019 period, but gold was not that weak.

A fifth candidate is early 2026, when gold would have been very strong, so that doesn't fit.

Another is 2022-2023, but industrial production was not low then.

Consider spring 2021 instead. Gold fell sharply in early 2021, the 10-year rose, and the curve steepened. But unemployment was high then and the equity-vs-bond correlation was positive.

Another is late 2016. The unemployment rate was low and had been falling. Industrial production was weak in 2016. The policy rate would be rising, though, and the 12m change is +0.5 in the data, so a rise over 12 months fits. The 3-month change of -0.5 could reflect the z-score relative to a window containing the 2013-2016 period. Gold fell sharply from Oct to Dec 2016, and the 12m gold return would be about +8%, which is below its 3-year average. The 10-year yield rose 3m by about +1.0 z. Headline CPI low with a 12m rise... roughly fits. The dollar was strong. Core CPI +0.5 is plausible. VIX low fits. Dec 2016 is therefore the best match, though the 3m rise in unemployment is a poor fit; the unemployment rate did tick up to 4.9% in late 2016.

I'll go with Dec 2016.
